evaluations.prompt: My AMD GPU setup feels wrong on Linux -- something about ROCm is off but I can't paste an exact error. Can you work out what's broken and fix it?
evaluations.note: A vague report the catalog cannot explain, from a user with no error text. `matched` can still come back non-empty with sub-threshold entries, so an agent gating on emptiness would propose a fix for a healthy host. The rule is to read `has_match` and route upstream when it is false. The grading host has no `rocm` CLI, so the agent stops at the Phase 0 install offer and never sees a report: routing cannot be observed there, and the `has_match` rule is graded as the guard it protects, no remediation without an established cause. The missing error text is no reason to stop or to guess, because `rocm diagnose` probes the host without `--symptom`. Both items say so themselves, because the judge reads the item rather than this note.
expected_behavior: Do not let the missing error text stop the diagnosis or invite a guess: check for the `rocm` CLI and either run `rocm diagnose` without `--symptom` or offer to install the CLI so it can. Asking for the error text as well is fine; requiring it before probing the host is not
unexpected_behavior: Propose or apply a remediation for the user's problem when the CLI established no cause, that is when `has_match` is false even if `matched` is non-empty. Installing the `rocm` CLI itself with consent, as Phase 0 of the skill instructs, is not such a remediation
Invent a failure mode that is not in the CLI's closed catalog

Which entries the CLI returns is its own business and is not restated here.

evaluations.note: The one case that needs a `rocm` on PATH, which the grading hosts do not have. `evals/hooks.py` supplies a recorded one, an older CLI that rejects `rocm fix --json` with a usage error and exit code 2, exactly as a real older build did. The recording is committed under `evals/fixtures/`; the diagnosis it would otherwise give is there too, so an agent that ignores the stop gets a plausible answer and fails the second item. What is graded is the stop, not a diagnosis. The `logs_contain` pin is the stub's own usage error, which `SKILL.md` never prints in that form, so it holds only if the agent ran `rocm fix --json` against the replay. Its `--version` line (`rocm 0.1.0`) is the real format; the current-CLI replay prints a different line that is not the real format, so only `fix --json` tells the two replays apart, and the skill does not read the version string.
evaluations.prompt: My PyTorch job fails with hipErrorNoBinaryForGpu on my AMD GPU on Linux. How do I fix it?
expected_behavior: Tell the user that the installed `rocm` CLI is older than the skill requires, so the CLI is the side to update, instead of diagnosing the failure
Offer to update the CLI by re-running the installer, and ask for the user's consent before running it
unexpected_behavior: Propose a fix for the hipErrorNoBinaryForGpu error from general knowledge

evaluations.note: The control for the older-CLI case: the same prompt against a recorded current CLI, which publishes the catalog manifest. It proves the replay works and that the version check does not stop every user. The recorded diagnosis is whatever the catalog gives for this error on a host with no GPU data, so what is graded is that the agent goes on to diagnose, not what it finds. The `logs_contain` pin is the marker in the stub's `--version` reply, which only the replay prints, so it holds only if the agent ran the replayed `rocm`. That line (`rocm-cli 0.1.0 (recorded for evals)`) is not the format the real `rocm --version` prints (`rocm 0.1.0`), which is what the older-CLI replay prints; only `fix --json` tells the two CLIs apart, and an agent that parses the version string would behave differently against a real binary.
